title: Lessee Accounting
description: Account for operating and finance leases from the lessee's perspective.
html:
Lessee Accounting

Under ASC 842, a lessee generally recognizes a right-of-use asset and a lease liability when a lease begins.

Core Idea:

The right-of-use asset represents the lessee's right to use the underlying asset, while the lease liability represents the obligation to make lease payments.

1. Initial Lease Liability

At lease commencement, the lease liability is generally measured at the present value of required lease payments that have not yet been paid.

Lease Liability = Present Value of Lease Payments

2. Right-of-Use Asset

The initial right-of-use asset generally begins with the initial lease liability and is adjusted for certain additional items.

Initial ROU Asset = Lease Liability + Lease Payments Made At or Before Commencement + Qualifying Initial Direct Costs − Lease Incentives Received
Example

Assume the initial lease liability is $90,000.

The lessee also made a $5,000 lease prepayment and received a $2,000 lease incentive.

$90,000 + $5,000 − $2,000 = $93,000 ROU Asset

3. Finance vs. Operating Lease

Lessees classify leases as either finance leases or operating leases.

A lease is classified as a finance lease when one or more of the applicable classification criteria are met.

Finance Lease Indicators

A lease is classified as a finance lease if one or more of the applicable classification criteria are met.

  • Ownership transfers to the lessee by the end of the lease term.
  • The lessee has a purchase option that it is reasonably certain to exercise.
  • The lease term represents a major part of the remaining economic life of the underlying asset.
  • The present value of lease payments and certain residual value guarantees equals or exceeds substantially all of the fair value of the underlying asset.
  • The underlying asset is so specialized that it is expected to have no alternative use to the lessor at the end of the lease.
Important:

ASC 842 does not require the old rigid 75% and 90% bright-line rules.

4. Finance Lease Expense Pattern

For a finance lease, interest on the lease liability and amortization of the ROU asset are generally presented separately.

Lease Liability Interest Expense
ROU Asset Amortization Expense

5. Operating Lease Expense Pattern

Operating leases are also generally recognized on the balance sheet with an ROU asset and lease liability.

However, the lessee generally recognizes a single lease expense, typically on a straight-line basis over the lease term.

Finance Lease Interest + Amortization
Operating Lease Generally Single Lease Expense

6. Short-Term Lease Election

A lessee may elect an accounting policy for qualifying short-term leases that avoids recognizing the ROU asset and lease liability.

A short-term lease generally has a lease term of 12 months or less at commencement and does not contain a purchase option that the lessee is reasonably certain to exercise.

7. Simple Present Value Example

Assume a lessee enters into a lease requiring three annual payments of $20,000.

The present value of those required payments at commencement is calculated to be $54,500.

Initial Lease Liability = $54,500

If there are no prepayments, incentives, or qualifying initial direct costs:

Initial ROU Asset = $54,500

CPA Exam Memory Rule

Lease Liability → PV of Lease Payments ROU Asset → Liability Adjusted for Prepayments / Incentives / Initial Direct Costs Finance Lease → Interest + Amortization Operating Lease → Generally Single Lease Expense

Key Takeaways

  • Lessees generally recognize an ROU asset and lease liability for both finance and operating leases.
  • The lease liability is initially based on the present value of lease payments.
  • The ROU asset begins with the lease liability and is adjusted for certain lease-related amounts.
  • Finance leases generally produce separate interest and amortization expense.
  • Operating leases generally produce a single lease expense.
  • Qualifying short-term leases may be eligible for a recognition exemption through an accounting policy election.

quiz.prompt: At lease commencement, a lessee records a lease liability of $120,000. The lessee also made a $6,000 prepayment and received a $4,000 lease incentive. Assume there are no initial direct costs. What is the initial right-of-use asset?
quiz.explanation: The initial ROU asset is generally the $120,000 lease liability plus the $6,000 prepayment minus the $4,000 incentive, giving $122,000.
